scope: Independent cell-level review of the current July 2024 Annex L matrix attachment only for cells relevant to generated PDF 2.0 merge-wrapper output, plus the explicitly corrected #83/#440 cells. This is not a full Table L.2 producer conformance audit or reader validation review.

attachment.provenance: Embedded primary EC3 physical p.962 / printed p.947 attachments. The grouped annotation states #64/#83/#336/#349/#440 corrected Annex L and the embedded matrices; its note says the July 2024 replacements supersede the earlier attachments. The current XLSX title is 'ISO 32000-2:2020 with errata (07-2024)'.

orientation.parent_axis: Column headings on spreadsheet row 2, C through AR.
orientation.child_axis: Child type labels in column B, rows 3 through 44.
orientation.cell_meaning: A cell gives the allowed occurrence for the child row under the parent column; the matrix is not symmetric. A relationship shown in the parent-type children view is repeated in the child-type parents view, not a reverse edge.
orientation.legend: Row 49 expands the symbols. Bare 1 means exactly once; 0..n means zero or more; ∅ means forbidden; ∅* means forbidden except when the parent is used as a grouping-level element; ‡ defers to the type-specific provisions.

features.clause: Annex L, Table L.2; #349 single-root note
features.source_location: Annex L begins primary physical p.962 / printed p.947. The current embedded XLSX cell C3 (child row Document, parent column StructTreeRoot) is '1'. The legend at row 49 defines bare 1 as exactly once. #349's primary annotation at p.963 clarifies StructTreeRoot is a dictionary, not a structure-element type.
features.effective_matrix: C3 = 1: exactly one Document child of StructTreeRoot. This agrees with the wrapper output's one /K child. No reverse-edge claim is made.
features.ledger: doc/conformance/ledger.toml row L, writer-side scope; §14.8.4.2 is separately implemented for role resolution, while no reader nesting validator is claimed.
features.implementation: pdf-transform/src/structure/wrapper.rs::Carry::wrap_documents selects top-level source elements whose role resolves to Document in the PDF 2.0 namespace (including role-mapped targets) and creates a wrapper only when at least two source documents contribute. pdf-transform/src/structure/write.rs::wrapper_element writes /S /Document, /NS, /P root, and /K source-Document references. The structure-root writer installs this wrapper as its single child. Grep of pdf-transform/src finds no other emitted PDF 2.0 standard Document type or general Table L.2 matrix validator. The PDF/A archive writer uses default PDF 1.7 namespace and is outside Annex L's PDF 2.0 condition.
tests_assertions: crates/pdf-transform/tests/merge.rs::two_pdf_2_0_documents_are_written_inside_one checks exactly one top-level child, its role and namespace as PDF 2.0 Document, two source Document children, each child's /P back to wrapper, structure check and archive judgements.

crates/pdf-transform/tests/annex_l_role_mapping.rs::role_mapped_pdf_2_documents_are_written_inside_one_document starts with custom DocAlias roles resolving to PDF 2.0 Document and checks exactly one wrapper plus its two mapped children and /P links; output must not be xref-recovered.
features.verdict: The exact generated root→Document relationship is admitted by C3 and has discriminating writer integration assertions, including the role-mapped population. The matrix does not test arbitrary source hierarchy, nor is such a reader rejection policy inferred.
features.residuals: The tests sample the only explicitly constructed PDF 2.0 standard Document wrapper edge found in the writer. They do not run a general checker over all cells or prove every derived output path preserves all source constraints. No such general checker was found in this inspection.

features.feature: Nested source Documents under the generated wrapper
features.source_location: Current embedded XLSX cell D3 (child row Document, parent column Document) is '0..n'. Row 49 defines this as zero or more occurrences.
features.effective_matrix: D3 = 0..n: a Document may contain zero or more Document children. The generated wrapper has two children in the integration tests. This is one directed parent Document→child Document relationship.
features.ledger: doc/conformance/ledger.toml row L and ADR 1474 describe the wrapper generated when PDF 2.0 Documents from multiple sources are merged.
features.implementation: wrapper_element writes the source Documents in /K in source order, and the carry/reconciliation path rewrites each source child's /P to the new wrapper. No unrelated current row/column intersection is treated as a reverse relationship.
features.tests_assertions: Both two_pdf_2_0_documents_are_written_inside_one and role_mapped_pdf_2_documents_are_written_inside_one require two source Document children beneath the synthetic wrapper and verify each child's /P points to that wrapper.
features.verdict: The generated child edge and its /P parent pointer agree with the effective D3 allowance; this independently checks that the wrapper does not merely satisfy C3 while placing source Documents outside it.
features.residuals: No claim about all Table L.2 pairs or malformed input-source relationships.

features.source_location: Primary physical p.962 / printed p.947 annotation #83: 'Table is now permitted as a child of P' and the matrix records this at both views. Current XLSX M33 = 0..n (child Table under parent P); AH10 = ∅ (child P under parent Table).
features.effective_matrix: M33 allows P→Table at 0..n; AH10 forbids the opposite Table→P relation. The two matrix perspectives in the PDF table repeat an edge, but these two XLSX cells are opposite directed pairs.
features.implementation: No generated wrapper path emits a P/Table pair; the relationship is source structure carried through. The writer currently has no general Table L.2 checker.
features.tests_assertions: The selected wrapper tests do not exercise M33/AH10; that is not a gap for the Document-wrapper behavior. No claim is made about whether all derived writer outputs preserve this pair.
features.verdict: Effective relation clarified: only P may parent Table, at 0..n. No Annex L implementation defect found in the merge wrapper from this erratum.
features.residuals: No full transform-path preservation test for P/Table; the source constraint is producer-facing, and a general writer audit is outside this bounded pass.

features.source_location: Primary physical pp.979 and 985 / printed pp.964 and 970 annotations #440 correct the WP/Figure cells. Current XLSX AC41 = 0..n (child Figure under parent WP); AP28 = ∅ (child WP under parent Figure).
features.effective_matrix: AC41 allows WP→Figure at 0..n. AP28 forbids Figure→WP. The previous undefined `c` marker is gone; neither this correction nor #83 creates symmetric relations.
features.implementation: No generated wrapper path emits a WP/Figure relationship; source hierarchy is carried. There is no general matrix validator in the inspected writer.
features.tests_assertions: Merge wrapper tests do not exercise AC41/AP28; their relevant edges are C3/D3. No failure follows from that test scope.
features.verdict: Current matrix has a well-defined, one-way optional WP→Figure relationship. No merge-wrapper mismatch.
features.residuals: No full writer validation/preservation test for WP/Figure in this bounded pass.

features.source_location: Primary physical p.962 group annotation names #336 among issues changing Annex L and its replacement matrices. The supplied current attachment is independently hashed and parsed, but no prior attachment version or standalone #336 cell-level annotation body was found in this worktree.
features.effective_matrix: The July 2024 matrix is authoritative for the reviewed current cells C3, D3, M33, AH10, AC41, AP28. This inspection cannot attribute any other current cell to #336 specifically or say which older cells it changed.
features.implementation: Only generated wrapper pairs C3/D3 were compared with current emitted output. Other cell effects were not mapped to code-generated relationships.
features.tests_assertions: The wrapper integration assertions cover C3/D3 only.
features.verdict: The source confirms #336 belongs to the correction group, but its individual matrix delta remains unknown here. Do not claim #336 is fully reviewed or assign it the #83/#440 semantics.
features.residuals: Individual #336 historical delta attribution is unknown. This does not block judging current cells against the effective attachment; remaining current cell/code-output comparisons are the conformance residual.
